All industries ↗

Connect office and field context

Construction and field service work generates schedules, daily reports, issue logs, photos, change questions, procurement updates, and client communication. Maia can prepare a concise exception list in Slack from records the team supplies.

The project manager, superintendent, trade partners, and qualified professionals make every safety, engineering, contractual, and sequencing decision.

Prepare the daily exception list

Provide the current schedule, daily report, issue log, selected photos, and owner map. Maia can identify newly blocked work, changed dates, unanswered questions, missing owners, and dependencies due soon.

Each item should link to its source and show the record timestamp. A photo can support an observation, but it should not become an engineering conclusion or safety determination.

Build an office-to-field handoff

When a decision made in the office affects site work, Maia can assemble the request, relevant drawings or records supplied by the team, current plan, expected answer, owner, and needed date.

The responsible lead confirms the instruction through the proper process. Maia helps make the handoff complete but does not authorize field work or replace formal document control.

Track submittal and procurement dependencies

Using an approved log and supplier updates, Maia can prepare items whose review or delivery now affects the schedule. It can show promised date, current date, downstream activity, and missing confirmation.

The project and procurement owners decide escalation, resequencing, or substitution. Maia does not approve a product or interpret technical compliance.

Draft stakeholder updates

Give Maia the confirmed status, milestone plan, client decisions, and project template. It can draft an internal or client update that separates completed work, current constraints, decisions needed, and next milestones.

The project leader verifies every date and external statement. Contract notices, claims, and formal instructions require their established review path.

Start with supplied project records

Choose one project review with a schedule conflict, a missing owner, and a photo tied to a daily report. Ask Maia to link the evidence, avoid visual conclusions, and prepare the question for the field lead.

The same exception format can support a morning coordination meeting. The project manager can sort items by area, trade, or required date, then assign the unresolved handoffs in the channel. At the next review, Maia can carry forward open items and remove work the team has confirmed complete.

For closeout, the workflow can shift to missing records, unresolved punch items, owner responses, and required handover documents. The project team still approves completion, while the brief gives office and field staff one place to see what remains.

Each item keeps its latest source date visible.

Questions from field teams

Can Maia interpret drawings or site photos?

It can organize supplied files and observations for review. Qualified professionals make technical, safety, code, and design judgments.

Can Maia update the project schedule?

It can propose exact changes when a supported action exists. The project manager reviews the sequencing, dates, and downstream impact.

Does Maia replace field or safety systems?

No. It prepares internal coordination in Slack. The owning project, safety, and document systems remain authoritative.
